 Judgment
This petition Under section 166 MV act is filed seeking compensation of Rs.12,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in a road traffic accident.
2. The brief facts of the petitioners case are as under: It is stated

that on 30.08.2021 at about 7.10 pm., when the petitioner was driving a vehicle bearing reg.No.KA-02-HU-8385 along with her sister by observing all traffic rules and regulations at 4th main road, Malleshwaram, at that time, the respondent No.1 driving his vehicle bearing reg.No.KA-52-Q- 4502 in a rash and negligent manner and came from 10 th cross and dashed the petitioner's vehicle.
Due to impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained injury.
Immediately after the accident, petitioner was shifted to Manipal Hospital, took treatment wherein she has spent more than Rs.50,000/-.
The petitioner has lodged a complaint at Malleshwaram police and filed the FIR and charge sheet at crime No.31/2021 for the offence punishable offence under Section 279 and 337 of IPC.

The accident occurred due to the rash and negligent manner of driving of the vehicle bearing reg.No.KA-52-Q-4502 by its driver and the Malleshwaram Traffic Police have registered a case in crime No.31/2021, after investigation the police have filed charge sheet against the said driver for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 337 of IPC.
The respondent No.1 to 3 are liable to pay compensation.
Hence, she has prayed to award compensation of Rs.5,00,000/- from the respondents.

3. In response to the petition notice, the Respondent No.2 and 3 have appeared before the court through their counsel and filed their written statement and Respondent No.1 did not appeared before the court and he was placed exparte.
4. Respondent No.2 - Insurance Company filed its objection denying the petition averments.
It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of offending vehicle and it was valid as on the date of accident.
It has also contended that the owner of the alleged offending vehicle and the concerned police have not complied the mandatory provisions of Sec.134(c) and 158(6) of MV Act.
However, its liability is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
It has denied the negligence of the driver of offending vehicle in causing the accident.
It has also denied the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner.
The compensation claimed is highly exorbitant.
For all these, it has prayed for dismissal of the petition.

4. Respondent No.3 - owner of the offending vehicle has filed her objection denying the petition averments as the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts and is liable to be dismissed in limine.

It is the contention of the respondent that, the petitioner was riding the alleged scooter bearing reg.No.KA-02-HU-8385 without knowledge of riding, without wearing helmet, without possessing valid vehicle documents in a rash and negligent manner at high speed without observing other vehicles.
Respondent denied the nature of accident and the petitioner was student.
Further respondent contended that, she was insured with respondent No.2.
For all these, it has prayed for dismissal of the petition.

2 5.

On the basis of the above pleadings of both the parties, my predecessor in office has framed the following issues: -
1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that on 30.08.2021 at about 7.10 pm., she was proceeding a bike bearing No.KA-02-HU-8385 as a rider along with her sister Sushmitha as a pillion rider, when they reached at 4th main road, Malleshwaram, at that time, the vehicle bearing reg.No.KA-52-Q-4502 being driven by its driver at high speed in a rash and negligent manner came and dashed against her motor cycle, as a result they fell on the ground and sustained grievous injuries, as mentioned in claim petition ?
2. Whether petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed in the petition ? If so,
from which respondent ?
3. What Order or Award ?

6. In order to prove the claim, the Petitioner examined herself as PW.1 and got marked 16 documents as per Ex.P.1 to P.16.
7.
The Respondent No.2 and 3 have not adduced rebuttal evidence.
8. I have heard the counsel on both sides and have perused the material on record.

9. My findings to the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2: Partly in affirmative.

Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:
REASONS 10. ISSUE NO.1:-
In order to prove her claim, the petitioner has relied on the police and medical records.
PW.1 is the injured and the direct witness to the incident.

She has deposed that on 30.08.2021 at about 7.10 pm., when she was driving a vehicle bearing reg.No.KA-02-HU-8385 along with her sister by observing all traffic rules and regulations at 4 th main road, Malleshwaram, at that time, the respondent No.1 driving his vehicle bearing reg.No.KA-52-Q-4502 in a rash and negligent manner and came from 10th cross and dashed to her.
Due to impact, she fell down and sustained injury.

11. In support of her claim she has produced copy of complaint at Ex.P1, FIR at Ex.P2 and charge sheet at Ex.P5.
12.
Respondent No.2- Insurance Company contended that the accident occurred due to sole negligence of the petitioner.
PW.1 has denied the same during cross examination.

The FIR and Rashmitha.A vs Rudresh on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/31242000/
3 charge sheet both are filed against the driver of offending vehicle.
Except the suggestion during cross examination and contention in the written statement of the Respondent, they have not produced any documentary evidence.
In the absence of documents to prove the negligence of the petitioner herself, it is held that it was the sole negligence of the driver of offending vehicle bearing reg.No.KA-52-Q-4502.
Police have filed charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle after complete investigation and the said charge sheet is not at all challenged by both the Respondents.
13. The evidence of PW-1 corroborates with the documents produced by her.
There is nothing elicited to disprove the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
From all the above documents, it is clear that the Petitioner sustained injuries in a road traffic accident that occurred only due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle.
Hence, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
14. ISSUE NO.2:- The Petitioner states that due to the accident she has sustained injuries to her left arm shoulder as well as left leg and spinal cord along with lacerated wounds.

Immediately she was shifted to Manipal hospital and she took treatment as an inpatient for which she has incurred the expenditure towards medical and other miscellaneous expenses and since she got injury to her spinal cord frequently diagnosis is required in future.
Further states that, she is an final year Engineering student studying at SAC college.
15. So far as the quantum of compensation is concerned, the Petitioner has sought for compensation of Rs.5,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by her in road traffic accident.
The PW.1 has produced 7 medical bills marked at Ex.P.13 amounting to Rs.18,837/- to show the expenses incurred by her.
16. The Petitioner says that she had suffered grievous injuries and took treatment as an inpatient.
In order to prove the same she has produced discharge summary at Ex.P.14 wherein it mentioned only date of admission, no mentioned date of discharge.

Wound certificate marked at Ex.P.12 wherein it shows that, she has suffered multiple contused abrasions present over the left foot and left elbow,
doctor has opined which is simple injury.
But there are no evidences that the Petitioner is suffering from any difficulties which would affect her livelihood and day- today activities.
In the absence of medical evidence to prove disability, I deem it proper to award global compensation.

By considering the nature of injuries, age of the petitioner, treatment taken in the hospital as stated supra and considering the pain and sufferings by the Petitioner, I deem it appropriate to award Rs.60,000/- as global compensation under all the conventional heads with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization.
17. Liability:

As it is already held that the accident was due to the negligence of driver of offending vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA- 52-Q-4502, the Respondent No.1 being the rider of offending vehicle,
respondent No.2 being the Insurance Company and respondent No.3 being RC owner of said vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioner.
Even though, insurance company has admitted the issuance of insurance policy and its validity in respect of the offending vehicle not challenged the liability.
Therefore, Respondent No.2 shall deposit the compensation amount with interest @ 6% p.a.
With these observations, I have answered Issue No.2 Partly in the affirmative.

4 18. ISSUE NO.3:

In view of the above discussion, reasons stated and findings given to Issue Nos. 1 &
2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Claim Petition filed under Sec.166 of M.V.Act is allowed in part with cost.

Petitioner is awarded compensation of Rs.65,000/- (Rupees sixty five thousand only)
together with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit with the Tribunal.
The respondents No.1 to 3 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
However, the respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the compensation amount in this tribunal within one month from the date of this order.
On deposit of the compensation amount, entire amount along with entire interest shall be released in favour of the Petitioner through E-payment on proper identification and verification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
(Dictated to the Stenographer directly on computer, corrected, signed and pronounced by me in open court dated this the 14th day of August 2024).
